title: "I've never seen anything scarier than an LLM with tool calls." — Erik Meijer aka @HeadinTheBox
talk_summary: Erik Meijer argues that LLM tool calls turn agents into unconstrained side-effecting loops (IO), and proposes deferring execution: the LLM emits a plan/program (a free-monad expression) that a separate trusted executor runs only after static checks (type checking, data-flow/taint analysis, proof) — i.e. proof-carrying code. The talk is conceptual/formal, not a product, but the core mechanism (separate planning from execution, inspect the plan before running it) is directly copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting the LLM run the agentic loop with tools, the model emits a plan/expression of the computation; a separate trusted component ("Bernie") executes it after checks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're air gapping the agentic loop from the agent. So we don't let the agent run the agentic loop. Before the agent run it, we want to be able to check it.

takeaways.technique: Static checks on the emitted program (type check + taint/data-flow analysis)
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the plan is a program (free monad / expression tree), you can run compiler-style analyses — type checking, data-flow, taint analysis — on it before execution, rather than reasoning about an opaque IO action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's trivial to do data flow analysis, type checking, and so on on programs. Right? So, now we're safe

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues LLM-as-judge for 'safe' is unformalizable; the fix is to make the artifact checkable (a program with a proof) so verification is mechanical, not another model opinion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's impossible to write a formal proof that an answer is safe or a question is proper. Um and that is why there are at least a hundred startups ... using LLMs as a judge

takeaways.technique: Least-privilege tool belt via deferred execution
takeaways.what_they_do: Moving IO to the executor shrinks the model's tool belt to plan-emission only, so the model can't directly mutate the world.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tool belt of Claude goes to the left to the left. And suddenly Claude is a nice puppy again

takeaways.what_they_do: The model's output is a program/expression representing the computation, not prose — designed for machines to generate, consume, and check.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we should stop designing languages for humans and it's all basic, only requires programming 101
